Compounding earns growth on earlier growth

Predict: at 10% per year, will year 5 wealth be £150 or more than £150?

Original hypothetical teaching example. This complete static route needs no JavaScript or animation. The interactive walkthrough is available inside the chapter.

On a narrow screen, scroll the diagram horizontally. Every value and step is also explained below.

Step 6/6: Year 5
Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £161.05; simple growth £150.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

All steps and numerical explanations

  1. Year 0

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £100.00; simple growth £100.00. Both begin at the same £100.

  2. Year 1

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £110.00; simple growth £110.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

  3. Year 2

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £121.00; simple growth £120.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

  4. Year 3

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £133.10; simple growth £130.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

  5. Year 4

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £146.41; simple growth £140.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

  6. Year 5

    Starting £100, constant 10% annual effective rate: compound £161.05; simple growth £150.00. Compound growth applies to the previous balance.

Assumed constant annual effective rate; no contributions, fees, taxes or inflation. Real investment returns are not fixed.
